resources.title: ETL Pipeline Design Checklist
resources.description: A pre-ship checklist from Chapter 6: is the load step idempotent (upsert, not append-only)? Does the watermark update only after a successful load, never before? Can the whole pipeline be safely rerun from the top after any failure? Each item ties back to the specific lesson that explains why it matters.

resources.chapterTitle: Logging, Testing, Error Handling and Automation
resources.title: Error Handling & Retry Pattern Reference
resources.description: The real patterns from Lesson 41 as copy-paste reference: catching specific exceptions instead of a bare except, exponential backoff for a flaky call, and the fail-loud-not-silent principle with a concrete before/after example — plus the non-zero exit status discipline that lets a scheduler actually detect a failed run.

resources.chapterTitle: Logging, Testing, Error Handling and Automation
resources.title: pytest Checklist for Data Validation Functions
resources.description: What to test and why, from Lesson 40: the good case, every real rejection case (not just one), and pytest.raises() for functions that should error — plus a reminder that a validation function tested only on good input can hide a bug in exactly the path a real pipeline depends on to catch bad data.

resources.title: Data Project Review Rubric
resources.description: A five-dimension rubric (correctness, testing, documentation, performance awareness, maintainability) for reviewing a finished Python ETL script or pipeline against a real professional standard. Shared across the Analytics Engineer path's courses.
